newsitem.title: UK: FULL TEXT-UK statement on pension companies.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-UK statement on pension companies.

text.p: Following is full text of a statement by Britain's Economic Secretary Helen Liddell on pension companies on Tuesday --
Pension companies have been warned to accelerate their review procedures without short cuts which would affect their customers, Helen Liddell, Economic Secretary said today.
Mrs Liddell was speaking on the day she published the responses from 24 of the pension companies which set out their strategies for speeding up the review of pension cases.
When she met the firms on 14 May, the Minister made clear that, in the public interest, progress would be reviewed each month and information published about progress being made by each firm.
The Minister has told pension companies that they must provide her with the information by 3 July. She has already indicated that if their action does not satisfy her, she will take further steps.

In reply to a Parliamentary Question from Stephen Timms MP (East Ham), the Minister said: "Some firms have already demonstrated that the pace of their reviews is quickening. I trust that this trend will accelerate ....

"While most of the policy statements sent to me showed a businesslike sense of purpose, I regret that there are two which appear to misunderstand the Government's determination that this matter must be resolved with dispatch.

"The Sedgewick Group is quite wrong to assert that the Government's initiative on 14 May was in any way under researched. And I am not convinced by the objections of the Board of Legal and General to well merited criticism of the industry's performance so far."
Mrs Liddell challenged the companies to better the targets for case review set by the Securities and Investment Board (SIB) and the Personal Investment Authority (PIA). The Minister said:
"Most of these replies suggest a willingness to deliver the targets for completion of case reviews set by the regulators.
"There are also some indications that firms are adopting, or considering, accelerated case management techniques which will improve the speed of case handling without prejudicing investors' rights.
"However, I shall be looking for evidence that firms are showing their sincerity and commitment to customer service while moving quickly to adopt such streamlined procedures."

The 24 companies involved are: Lloyds Abbey Life, Allied Dunbar, Barclays, Britannic, Colonial, Co-operative Insurance, Equitable Life, GAN, Guardian Royal, Hogg Robinson, Legal and General, Lincoln International, Lloyds/TSB, London and Manchester, NatWest, Norwich Union, Pearl, Prudential, Royal Sun Alliance, Royal London, Sedgewick, Sun Life of Canada, United Assurance and Windsor Life.
